title: The day The Hawthorns opened.
deck: Four months of construction. More than a century of memories.
imageNote: The ground pictured in December 2013, not on opening day.
body: The Hawthorns opened on 3 September 1900 after construction lasting just four months. The first fixture ended 1–1 against Derby County. Steve Bloomer scored for Derby; Chippy Simmons equalised for Albion.

The club initially held a lease and bought the freehold in 1913. Hawthorn bushes had grown on the estate, giving the new ground a name that became part of Albion’s identity. Today’s ground looks very different, but the site has carried the club’s home matches since that opening afternoon.
